```{r}
# Walksheds Dataframe
```

  # Downloading Census Data

```{r}
tracts <- get_decennial(geography = "tract",
                           variables = "H1_001N",
                           state = params$states,
                           year = 2020,
                           geometry = TRUE)
```

  

```{r}
# Median income in past 12 months: B06011_001 (individual income), B19013_001 (household income)

income <- get_acs(
  state = params$states,
  geography = "tract",
  variables = "B19013_001",
  geometry = TRUE,
  output = "wide",
  year = 2020)

income <- st_drop_geometry(income)
```

https://api.census.gov/data/2020/dec/pl/groups/P2.html

```{r}
white_p <- get_decennial(
  state = params$states,
  geography = "tract",
  variables = "P2_005N",
  geometry = TRUE,
  output = "wide",
  year = 2020)

# previously used B02001_002 (and was set to get_acs)

white_p <- st_drop_geometry(white_p)

white_population <- sum(white_p$P2_005N)

white_population
```

```{r}
walksheds_demo_df <- walksheds_df |>
  left_join(income |> select(GEOID, B19013_001E), by = "GEOID") |>
  left_join(white_p |> select(GEOID, P2_005N), by = "GEOID") |>
  left_join(black_p |> select(GEOID, P2_006N), by = "GEOID") |>
  left_join(hispanic_p |> select(GEOID, P2_002N), by = "GEOID") |>
  left_join(asian_p |> select(GEOID, P2_008N), by = "GEOID")
```

```{r}
walksheds_demo_df <- walksheds_demo_df |>
  rename(household_income = B19013_001E) |>
  rename(white_p = P2_005N) |>
  rename(black_p = P2_006N) |>
  rename(hispanic_p = P2_002N) |>
  rename(asian_p = P2_008N)
```

```{r}
bw_pops <- walksheds_demo_df[, c("white_p", "black_p")]

bw_pops <- st_drop_geometry(bw_pops)
```

# Segregation Data

https://syunhong.github.io/seg/
tldr: seg and dissim functions should operate the same/similarly; also they do not consider census tracts/spatial arrangements

```{r}
segregation_index <- dissim(data = bw_pops)

segregation_index

# keep all rows but only use column: [, 1:2]
```

- Use diversity index for the census tracts themselves? Since the dissimilarity index cannot be applied to each census tract.

```{r}
diversity_measure <- diversity(bw_pops, index = "shannon", MARGIN = 1, base = exp(1)) |>
  data.frame()

diversity_measure

# simpson is used for US Census Data Diversity Index
```

```{r}
diversity_measure_table <- walksheds_demo_df |>
  mutate(diversity(bw_pops, index = "shannon", MARGIN = 1, base = exp(1))) |>
  rename(diversity_value = `diversity(bw_pops, index = "shannon", MARGIN = 1, base = exp(1))`)
  # 
  # diversity(walksheds_demo_df, index = "simpson", MARGIN = 1, base = exp(1))

diversity_measure_table

# use shannon or simpson or invsimpson measure
# for shannon, see how a better version should be used: https://github.com/konopinski/Shannon
```

```{r}
ggplot(diversity_measure_table, aes(fill = diversity_value)) + 
  geom_sf() + 
  theme_void() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "turbo") +
labs(fill = "Diversity Index Value")
```

```{r}
RUCA_exclude <- c(2:6)

RUCA_1_tracts <- diversity_measure_table |>
  filter(!(PrimaryRUCA %in% RUCA_exclude))

ggplot(RUCA_1_tracts, aes(fill = diversity_value)) + 
  geom_sf() + 
  theme_void() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "turbo") +
labs(fill = "Diversity Index Value")
```

Note: For Detroit, the tracts with a 1.00 diversity index value have a population of 0-4, hence the importance of population weights (and then make a heat map to visualize it more accurately?)

```{r}
RUCA_1_tracts_transformed <- RUCA_1_tracts |>
  st_transform(3857)

cartogram_data <- cartogram_cont(RUCA_1_tracts_transformed,
                 weight = "PopulationCount")

# https://r-charts.com/spatial/cartogram-ggplot2/
```


```{r}
ggplot(cartogram_data, aes(fill = diversity_value)) +
  geom_sf() +
  theme_void() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "turbo")
```

```{r}
walkshed_data_cartog_dorling <-cartogram_dorling(RUCA_1_tracts_transformed,
                    weight = "PopulationCount")
```

```{r}
ggplot(walkshed_data_cartog_dorling, aes(fill = diversity_value)) +
  geom_sf() +
  theme_void() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "turbo")
```
